the molecular response of rumen and colon to increasing grain levels involves coordinated alterations in mRNA expression of epithelial transporters and the Na+/K+-pump to maintain epithelial homeostasis and nutrient absorption.

The main takeaway from our work is that
rumen and colonic epithelium of goats fed a high-grain diet exhibit coordinated molecular changes in nutrient transport and ion gradients to adapt to the increased grain levels in the diet.

high grain diets may have a negative effect on epithelial integrity of the rumen and colon, which may be related to a decrease in the expression of Na+/K+- and glucose-transporting systems and a decrease in the absorption of glucose.
